title: ‘Sapta Dhara’ Roadmap: 7 Pillars Set Out for Viksit Bharat by 2047
content:
# ‘Sapta Dhara’ Roadmap: 7 Pillars Set Out for Viksit Bharat by 2047

Written by: Team Angel OneUpdated on:  16 Aug 2026, 12:20 am IST

Sapta Dhara sets seven development priorities for India by 2047, including manufacturing, food processing, technology and infrastructure.

Share

India’s plan for becoming a developed nation by 2047 has been linked to a seven-pillar framework called “Sapta Dhara”, as per a Business Standard news report.  

The framework was outlined in the 80th Independence Day address and covers manufacturing, agriculture and food processing, technology, infrastructure, defence, the green and blue economy, and soft power. 

No new schemes or specific policy measures were announced with the framework. Instead, the seven pillars set out the areas identified for economic and development priorities over the coming years. 

## **Manufacturing Target**

Manufacturing is the first pillar, with cost, quality and scale listed as the main areas of focus. The sector currently accounts for around 17% of India’s GDP. 

The government wants manufacturing’s share of GDP to reach 25% by 2035. The sector is also being positioned as part of India’s plans to increase its share of global production and attract investment into manufacturing. 

## **Agriculture and Food Processing**

Agriculture and food processing form the second pillar. The focus is on adding value to agricultural products and increasing the scope for processed food exports. 

The framework also points to the market access available through free trade agreements. India has put FTAs with Oman and the UK into effect during the current financial year.  

An agreement with the European Union is expected to be signed by December and become effective in the first half of next year. 

## **Technology and Infrastructure**

Technology and innovation are the third pillar, covering semiconductors, artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure and other emerging technologies. 

The fourth pillar, Gati Shakti, relates to infrastructure and logistics. Defence power is the fifth pillar, with self-reliance in arms manufacturing as its focus. The sixth covers the green and blue economy, including sustainable growth and marine resources. 

## **Soft Power**

Soft power forms the seventh pillar and includes India’s cultural, diplomatic and global influence. The seven areas cover production, farming, technology, infrastructure, defence, sustainability and international influence. 

## **Conclusion**

The framework does not specify funding, individual schemes, or implementation timelines. It serves as a broad outline of the areas being considered as India works towards the 2047 development target.

title: PM Modi unveils 'Shakti Ki Saptadhara', outlines seven pillars of India's growth - DD India
content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday unveiled ‘Shakti Ki Saptadhara’, outlining seven key strengths that he said will drive India’s next phase of growth and shape the country’s journey towards Viksit Bharat.

Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the occasion of India’s 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said the seven pillars would provide the foundation for India’s future development.

The first pillar, he said, is manufacturing, calling for India to emerge as a reliable hub in global supply chains.

“From Design to Manufacturing, India must become a reliable hub in the global supply chain. For this, I want to place special emphasis on three things. My brothers and sisters in the field of Manufacturing, do not let this opportunity slip away. For this, we will have to meet global standards on cost, quality, and scale,” he said.

The second strength, PM Modi said, is agriculture and food processing. He called for India’s farmers and food products to gain a larger presence in global markets, particularly as free trade agreements open access to new markets.

“We must go from the farm to the export market. Our traditional cuisine, millets, spices, and fruits and flowers should become global brands,” he said.

Technology and innovation constitute the third pillar of ‘Saptadhara’, according to the Prime Minister.

Highlighting the growing importance of artificial intelligence, quantum technology, space, robotics and data centres, PM Modi said India must establish itself as a global hub of innovation.

He highlighted India’s achievements in UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure and called for the country to take the next leap in next-generation communication technologies, including Made-in-India 6G.

The fourth pillar is Gati Shakti, with the Prime Minister calling for seamless and high-speed connectivity across the country.

“We need seamless high-speed rail connectivity, modern highway connectivity, inland waterways, airports, multi-modal logistics hubs and ports. We have to work towards port-led development,” he said.

Defence production is the fifth pillar, with PM Modi stressing the need for self-reliance and for India to emerge as a global supplier of defence equipment and technologies.

“It is essential to be self-reliant in the defence sector; this has now been experienced by both India and the world. When the world is immersed in its own thoughts, India cannot remain merely a market for the world. We must become self-reliant in the field of defence,” he said.

He called for the development of next-generation defence technologies to strengthen India’s position as a global supplier.

The sixth pillar, PM Modi said, is green energy. He called for greater innovation in renewable energy, energy storage and green hydrogen, while also highlighting opportunities in the Blue Economy.

“India must achieve global leadership in green hydrogen, renewable energy and energy storage, while continuing to provide solutions to global challenges. The Blue Economy, too, offers immense opportunities in fisheries, coastal tourism and ocean technology, opening new pathways for India’s growth,” he said.

The seventh strength of ‘Saptadhara’ is India’s soft power, with PM Modi highlighting Yoga, Ayurveda, handicrafts, culture, films, animation, gaming and digital content.

“Today, Yoga has connected the world to India. Our Ayurveda, holistic healthcare, handicrafts, culture, films, animation, gaming, digital content. The world is recognizing and looking forward to India’s WAVES summit,” he said.

He also highlighted India’s national parks and said the country’s cultural and natural heritage could help attract more international tourists.

Earlier, PM Modi hoisted the National Flag at the Red Fort. The flag hoisting was synchronised with a 21-gun salute by the 1721 Field Battery (Ceremonial), which used indigenous 105 mm Light Field Guns.

-ANI

The world's markets are now open for our farmers. Because of FTAs, we are getting access to a very large market, and we must reach there. We need to go from the farm to the export market. Our traditional food, millets, spices, and fruits and vegetables should become global brands." ## 3. We need seamless high-speed rail connectivity, modern highway connectivity, inland waterways, airports, multi-modal logistics hubs and ports. We have to work towards port-led development. The fifth 'shakti' is Defence production, in which we must become self-reliant and aim to become a global supplier." ## 5. "By developing Next Generation Defence Technology, we must move forward in the direction of becoming a global supplier," he added. ## 6. title: Decoding 'Saptadhara': The 7 Pillars of PM Modi's 2047 Vision
content:
India News

# Decoding 'Saptadhara': The 7 Pillars of PM Modi's 2047 Vision

* Edited by: Anurag Kumar
* Updated Aug 15, 2026, 09:04 IST

## What will power India's rise by 2047? PM Modi's 'Saptadhara' lays out seven pillars - from manufacturing and AI to defence, green energy and soft power - that could reshape India's growth story.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the nation during the 8oth Independence Day celebrations, at Red Fort in New Delhi.

Photo : PTI

follow usfollow us

**New Delhi:** Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 80th Independence Day speech was not just a look back at India's journey since Independence - it was a blueprint for where he wants the country to go by 2047. At the heart of that vision was 'Saptadhara', seven streams of India's energy, strength and willpower that PM Modi said can drive the country towards self-reliance and developed-nation status.

From factories and farms to artificial intelligence, defence, green energy and India's cultural influence, the seven pillars span almost every major engine of India's future economy. PM Modi called on citizens and businesses to harness these strengths to make India more self-reliant and competitive globally.

## Here is a closer look at the seven pillars of PM Modi's 'Saptdhara':

**1. Manufacturing: The Engine Of Future Growth**

Manufacturing was the first pillar of 'Saptadhara', with PM Modi calling for a major expansion of India's manufacturing capabilities.

"We need components as well as complete product," PM Modi said, stressing the need for India to become a key part of global supply chains.

He urged the manufacturing sector to focus on cost, quality and scale to compete globally.

"Our packaging should attract people, and our precision should become our identity," Modi said.

The broader message was clear: India must move beyond assembling products and build the components, technologies and finished goods that global markets need.

**2. Kisan: Food And Farming**

The second pillar is India's farm and food sector.

PM Modi identified farmers and agriculture as a key part of the country's future growth, highlighting the need to strengthen India's food and farming ecosystem.

The focus on agriculture also places India's farmers at the centre of the country's broader goal of becoming self-reliant.

**3. Technology: From UPI To 6G**

Technology and innovation form the third pillar of 'Saptadhara'.

"It is the age of data centres, robotics and emerging technologies. So, India will have to be the hub of these technologies. We have realised our potential through the introduction of UPI. We have to aim that Made in India's 6G reaches across the country," PM Modi said.

From data centres and robotics to 6G, PM Modi's message was that India must not merely consume new technologies but develop them and emerge as a global technology hub.

**4. Gati Shakti: Building At Speed**

The fourth pillar is Gati Shakti, or the ability to move people, goods and businesses faster through better infrastructure and connectivity.

PM Modi stressed the need for more roads and expressways to improve connectivity and give businesses a boost.

The focus on speed and infrastructure is closely linked to India's ambitions to strengthen logistics, attract investment and become a more competitive manufacturing and trade hub.

**5. Raksha Shakti: Building India's Defence Muscle**

The fifth pillar is Raksha Shakti, with Modi making a strong pitch for self-reliance in defence manufacturing.

He called for greater domestic defence production and highlighted the importance of emerging technologies such as drones and counter-drone systems.

The message was to reduce dependence on foreign suppliers while building India's own defence capabilities and technologies.

**6. Green Energy: Powering The Next Growth Phase**

Green energy forms the sixth pillar of 'Saptadhara'. PM Modi called for greater innovation in the green energy sector as India seeks to meet its growing energy needs while moving towards cleaner sources of power.

The emphasis on green energy also fits into India's larger ambition of combining economic growth with energy security and a lower-carbon future.

**7. Soft Power: India's Global Influence**

The seventh and final pillar is India's soft power.

PM Modi pointed to yoga, handicrafts, films, animation, gaming, digital content and the wider creative economy as areas through which India can expand its global cultural influence.

He also highlighted India's tourism potential, saying the country has the ability to attract visitors from around the world.

From national parks and cultural destinations to India's creative industries, Modi said these assets can become powerful drivers of India's global influence and economic growth.

## What 'Saptadhara' Means For India's 2047 Goal

Together, the seven streams - manufacturing, farmers, technology, Gati Shakti, Raksha Shakti, green energy and soft power - form the economic, technological, strategic and cultural framework of PM Modi's 'Saptadhara' vision.

The idea fits into the larger ambition laid out in his 80th Independence Day address: an India that is self-reliant, technologically advanced, economically powerful and developed by 2047, when the country marks 100 years of Independence.

title: Saptadhara PM Modi’s 7-Point Vision for Viksit Bharat 2047, Latest News
content:
Saptadhara is PM Modi’s seven-point vision for Viksit Bharat, focusing on manufacturing, agriculture, technology, Gati Shakti, defence, green-blue economy and soft power.

By Abhishek Singh - Aug 15, 2026, 11:35 IST

Listen

Copied!

## **Saptadhara Vision Latest News**

Saptadhara is a seven-point development vision announced by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi on India’s 80th Independence Day, August 15, 2026**. It focuses on **manufacturing, agriculture and food processing, technology and innovation, Gati Shakti, defence, green and blue economy, and soft power** as key drivers of India’s future growth. The framework aims to strengthen India’s economic and strategic capabilities and accelerate the country’s journey towards **Viksit Bharat**. 

## **PM Modi’s ‘Saptadhara’ Vision for Viksit Bharat**

* On **India’s 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026**, Prime Minister Narendra Modi introduced the **‘Saptadhara’**, meaning **seven streams of strength**, as a broad roadmap for India’s future growth and development.
* The vision focuses on seven important areas – **manufacturing, agriculture and food processing, technology and innovation, Gati Shakti, defence, green and blue economy, and soft power**.
* PM Modi said these seven areas can provide a strong base for the journey towards **Viksit Bharat** by improving India’s economic strength, technological capabilities, infrastructure, security and global influence.
* Referring to the idea of **‘Sapta Sindhu’**, he described Saptadhara as a new flow of national strength that can help India achieve in the next **5-7 years** what could not be achieved over several previous decades.

## **PM Modi’s 7-Point Saptadhara Agenda**

* **Manufacturing:** The first focus is on making Indian manufacturing more competitive in terms of **cost, quality and scale**. The aim is to strengthen domestic production and help Indian products meet global standards and compete in international markets.
* **Agriculture and Food Processing:** The vision gives importance to modernising agriculture, increasing the value of farm products and improving food processing. Greater focus on **global markets and Indian agricultural brands** can help raise farmers’ incomes and expand India’s agricultural exports.
* **Technology and Innovation:** Technology is seen as a major driver of future growth. The focus includes strengthening **digital technologies, communication systems, scientific research and emerging technologies** to build a more innovative and competitive economy.
* **Gati Shakti:** This stream focuses on improving **connectivity, mobility and infrastructure**. Faster transport networks and better coordination between different modes of transportation can make the movement of people and goods more efficient while supporting economic activity.
* **Defence:** Under **Raksha Shakti**, the emphasis is on greater **self-reliance in defence technology and production**. India aims to strengthen domestic capabilities in areas such as advanced defence systems, drones and next-generation technologies.
* **Green and Blue Economy:** PM Modi highlighted the potential of India’s **natural resources, environment and coastal assets** to support sustainable growth. The focus is on combining economic development with cleaner energy, environmental sustainability and opportunities linked to the blue economy.
* **Soft Power:** The final stream focuses on India’s global influence through its **culture, traditions, knowledge systems and creative sectors**. Areas such as **Yoga, Ayurveda, holistic health, tourism and creative industries** can strengthen India’s international image and cultural reach.

## **Why is Saptadhara Important for Viksit Bharat?**

* The Saptadhara**framework** presents development as a combined effort across the economy, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, sustainability and global influence rather than depending on a single sector.
* Its emphasis on **manufacturing, technology and defence self-reliance** reflects the broader goal of building a stronger and more resilient Indian economy with greater domestic capabilities.
* The focus on **green growth and the blue economy** also links development with sustainability, while the soft-power component highlights India’s ability to use its cultural and civilisational strengths on the global stage.
* Overall, PM Modi presented Saptadhara as a **next-generation development framework** aimed at giving India greater momentum and helping accelerate the country’s journey towards **Viksit Bharat**.

# PM Modi Unveils Sapta Dhara Framework for Viksit Bharat

August 15, 2026




Prime Minister Narendra Modi introduced the seven-pillar Sapta Dhara framework during the 80th Independence Day address from the Red Fort in New Delhi on 15 August 2026. The framework sets a national target of Viksit Bharat by 2047 and groups growth priorities into seven streams covering industry, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, energy, and soft power.

#### Sapta Dhara Framework

Sapta Dhara is also referred to as Shakti Ki Saptadhara. The seven streams named in the framework are manufacturing, agriculture and food processing, technology and innovation, Gati Shakti, self-reliance in defence, the green and blue economy, and India’s soft power.

Gati Shakti is a logistics and infrastructure planning approach used for integrated connectivity and project coordination. The green economy covers low-carbon development, while the blue economy relates to the sustainable use of ocean and marine resources.

#### Manufacturing, Technology and Defence

The manufacturing component places emphasis on cost, quality, and scale. These three terms are commonly used in industrial policy to refer to price competitiveness, product standards, and production capacity.

The technology and innovation stream includes a mission-mode plan to train 1 crore youth in Artificial Intelligence over the next year. Artificial Intelligence is a branch of computer science that enables machines to perform tasks such as learning, pattern recognition, and language processing.

The defence stream refers to self-reliance in defence, a policy area linked with domestic production of military equipment, platforms, and systems.

#### Energy Security and Urban Gas Network

India has set a target of 100 GW nuclear energy capacity by 2047. Nuclear energy is produced through controlled fission reactions in reactors, and India operates both pressurised heavy water reactors and imported light water reactor technology.

Five new nuclear reactors are scheduled to become operational in the next six to seven years. India’s domestic piped natural gas network has expanded from 70 cities 12 years ago to more than 700 cities, with 1.75 crore households connected.

> #### Important Facts for Exams
>
> * India observes Independence Day on 15 August every year, and the main ceremony is held at the Red Fort in New Delhi.
> * Viksit Bharat refers to the goal of making India a developed nation by 2047, the centenary year of Independence.
> * Gati Shakti is associated with integrated planning for transport, logistics, and infrastructure projects.
> * The blue economy is linked with fisheries, ports, shipping, offshore energy, and marine resources.

#### Soft Power and Long-Term Goals

Soft power refers to influence through culture, values, education, and diplomacy rather than military force. The framework places soft power among the seven streams of national growth.

The 2047 target year coincides with 100 years of India’s Independence. The framework was presented as part of the Independence Day address on 15 August 2026.

title: PM Modi Unveils ‘Sapta Dhara’ Vision For India’s Next Growth Phase
content:
## Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled the **‘Sapta Dhara’** framework in his Independence Day address, outlining seven streams of strength for India’s next growth phase. The pillars cover manufacturing, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, green and blue economies, and soft power, with the broader goal of building a developed and self-reliant India.

### Key Highlights

* PM Modi unveiled **‘Sapta Dhara’**, or Seven Streams, as a framework for India’s next growth phase.
* The seven pillars cover **manufacturing, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, green and blue economy, and soft power**.
* He called for India to become a **trusted global supply-chain and innovation hub** while strengthening defence self-reliance.
* The Prime Minister linked the vision to the broader goal of building a **‘Viksit Bharat’** over the coming years.

### **New Delhi, August 15, 2026:** Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address from the Red Fort, unveiled the concept of **‘Sapta Dhara’ (Seven Streams)**, identifying seven key areas that he said would provide India with the strength and momentum needed to enter its next phase of growth and achieve the vision of **‘Viksit Bharat’**.

Drawing a parallel with the historical concept of **‘Sapta Sindhu’ (Seven Rivers)**, PM Modi said India now needs a new current of development and national strength to realise its aspirations as a developed nation.

He said the next **five to seven years** would be particularly significant and that the combined strength of the seven streams could enable India to achieve in the coming years what had remained difficult to accomplish over several previous decades.

The Prime Minister also stressed that India’s young population would be central to this transformation, with the capabilities and potential of the youth to be fully harnessed for nation-building.

### 1. Manufacturing Power

The first stream of **Sapta Dhara** is Manufacturing Power. PM Modi called for a major expansion of India’s manufacturing capabilities, covering everything from micro-components to large finished products.

He emphasised the importance of developing complete value chains within India, from product design and component manufacturing to finished goods, with the objective of establishing the country as a **trusted global supply-chain hub**.

He urged manufacturers, entrepreneurs and MSMEs to use the opportunity to expand India’s presence in international markets while meeting global standards for **cost, quality and scale**.

The Prime Minister also called for precision manufacturing and a **‘Zero Defect’** approach, stressing that quality must remain non-negotiable.

### 2. Agriculture and Food Production

The second stream focuses on **Agriculture and Food Production**, along with large-scale food processing.

PM Modi said expanding global markets are creating new opportunities for Indian farmers and stressed the need to connect farm production with international demand.

He called for India to bridge the gap between the **farm and export market**, while expanding food processing and adding greater value to agricultural products.

### 3. Technology and Innovation

The third stream is **Technology and Innovation**, which PM Modi described as crucial in an era shaped by Artificial Intelligence, quantum technology, space, robotics and data centres.

He said India should not remain merely a consumer market for emerging technologies but should position itself as a **global hub of innovation**.

Referring to India’s experience with **UPI and digital public infrastructure**, the Prime Minister said India should take its digital public technologies to countries and communities across the world.

### 4. Gati Shakti and Infrastructure

The fourth stream is **Gati Shakti**, representing infrastructure and seamless connectivity.

PM Modi called for high-speed and integrated connectivity across India, including high-speed rail, modern highways, inland waterways, advanced airports and multimodal logistics networks.

The objective, he said, should be to build infrastructure that connects cities, industries, markets and communities efficiently while strengthening India’s economic competitiveness.

### 5. Raksha Shakti and Defence

The fifth stream is **Raksha Shakti, or Defence Power**.

PM Modi said achieving **Aatmanirbharta in defence** is essential for India’s security and strategic autonomy. He stressed that India should move beyond being an arms market and develop the capabilities needed to become a **global defence supplier**.

He highlighted the importance of next-generation technologies, including drones, counter-drone systems and hypersonic defence capabilities.

The Prime Minister also identified cybersecurity as an increasingly important component of national security and said India’s young talent could contribute to protecting both India and the wider world.

### 6. Green and Blue Economy

The sixth stream combines the **Green Economy and Blue Economy**.

PM Modi called for India to achieve global scale in areas such as **green hydrogen, renewable energy, energy storage, green mobility and green manufacturing**.

He said the transition towards a green economy could also generate substantial employment through the expansion of green jobs.

The Prime Minister also highlighted India’s coastline and the opportunities offered by the blue economy. Fisheries, coastal tourism and ocean technologies, he said, could become important contributors to India’s future economic growth.

### 7. India’s Soft Power

The seventh and final stream is **Soft Power**, which PM Modi described as an area with enormous potential for India and the world.

He highlighted the global reach of **Yoga**, as well as India’s strengths in Ayurveda, holistic healthcare, handicrafts, culture, films and the wider creative economy.

The Prime Minister also pointed to opportunities in **VFX, animation, gaming and digital content**, saying India can establish a stronger global presence in the creative economy.

He cited the **WAVES Summit (World Audio Visual & Entertainment Summit)** as an important platform for showcasing India’s creative talent and soft power to the world.

### Youth at the Centre of the Seven Streams

Across the seven pillars, PM Modi placed particular emphasis on India’s youth, calling for their energy, talent and capabilities to be integrated into the country’s development journey.

The framework seeks to bring together India’s manufacturing capacity, agricultural strength, technological capabilities, infrastructure, defence ecosystem, environmental opportunities and cultural influence into a broader national growth strategy.

## Through the **‘Sapta Dhara’** framework, Prime Minister Narendra Modi outlined seven interconnected streams that he said can power India’s next phase of development. From manufacturing and agriculture to technology, infrastructure, defence, green and blue economies, and soft power, the vision seeks to combine economic strength with technological capability, strategic self-reliance and India’s global cultural influence.

The framework forms part of the larger ambition of building a **‘Viksit Bharat’**, with the Prime Minister identifying the next five to seven years as a critical period for translating India’s potential into sustained national growth and global competitiveness.

content:
# Sapta Dhara Will Build India. Talent Will Build Sapta Dhara.

The Sapta Dhara vision articulated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in his Independence Day address is a powerful framework for India’s next phase of growth.

Manufacturing. Agriculture & Food. Technology & Innovation. Gati Shakti. Raksha. Green & Blue Economy. Soft Power.

These are not merely seven sectors. They are seven engines that can propel India towards becoming a globally competitive and developed nation.

But there is one fundamental question:

Who will build the talent capable of powering these seven Dharas?

I believe India's educational institutions have an opportunity—and a responsibility—to become active partners in this transformation.

### A Sapta Dhara for Institutions

Industry Dhara — Bring real businesses, GCCs, startups and industry problems into the campus.

Innovation Dhara — Move beyond academic projects towards solving real-world problems, creating IP and building new ventures.

Skills Dhara — Continuously develop capabilities in AI, emerging technologies, domain expertise and future skills.

Entrepreneurship Dhara — Make entrepreneurship a lived campus experience by bringing entrepreneurs and real ventures into institutions.

Global Dhara — Prepare students to work confidently across countries, cultures and global organisations.

Impact Dhara — Measure institutional success through employability, innovation, entrepreneurship and real-world outcomes.

### Communication Dhara — A National Priority

This deserves special attention.

If India wants to go global, Indian talent cannot be seen as incomplete professionals because they struggle to communicate their knowledge, ideas and capabilities.

A technically brilliant engineer who cannot articulate an idea.

A management graduate who cannot influence a stakeholder.

A scientist who cannot present research globally.

A young professional who cannot participate confidently in an international meeting.

These are not merely “soft-skill gaps”. They are capability gaps.

Communication Skill Development therefore cannot remain a conventional module delivered before placements.

Institutions need to take it on a war footing.

It must become a continuous capability-building journey—integrated with academic learning, projects, internships, presentations, teamwork, interviews and real-world professional experiences.

Because India's ambition is global.

Our talent must be global-ready.

The Prime Minister has articulated the national vision through Sapta Dhara.

It is now for India's institutions to build the talent architecture that can turn that vision into reality.

Sapta Dhara will build India. Talent will build Sapta Dhara.

What should the 8th Dhara for Institutions be?

title: PM Modi invokes Saptadhara in I-Day speech:  What is his 7-point vision for Viksit Bharat, and is it inspired by Hinduism?
content:
* English News

* PM Modi Saptadhara Vision | Viksit Bharat & Hindu Tradition Analysis

# Explained PM Modi invokes Saptadhara in I-Day speech:What is his 7-point vision for Viksit Bharat, and is it inspired by Hinduism?

14 hours ago

* Copy link

When Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled his vision of ‘Saptadhara’ from the ramparts of the Red Fort during his speech on the 80th Independence Day, he was not coining a slick new buzzword. He was reaching deep into Hindu tradition and repurposing a concept that has carried spiritual weight for centuries, giving it a fresh, economic life.

Saptadhara is a compound of two Sanskrit words: sapta, meaning seven, and dhara, meaning stream or flow. The prime minister used it to describe seven strategic pillars he believes can carry India towards becoming a developed nation by 2047.

**Where the idea comes from**

The number seven occupies a special place in Hindu thought. It appears in the Saptarishis, the seven revered sages; in cosmological descriptions of seven worlds; and, most relevantly here, in the idea of seven sacred rivers, or Sapta Sindhu, an ancient geographical and cultural marker of the early Vedic world.

There is also a more specific precedent. The Padma Purana describes a site called Saptadhara-tirtha, associated with the sages and linked to seven auspicious streams regarded as forms of the Ganga.

The same text connects the location to the Pandavas, reinforcing its sanctity. Elsewhere, local tradition at Haridwar holds that the Ganga split into seven channels so the Saptarishis could meditate undisturbed by the river's flow.

Across these accounts, "seven streams" consistently symbolises abundance, sanctity and the dispersal of a single powerful force in multiple directions, themes of completeness rather than division.

It is this layered symbolism, rather than any single textual source, that gives Saptadhara its resonance: a term already understood in Indian households as denoting wholeness and plurality flowing from one origin.

**From sacred rivers to a modern roadmap**

Modi invoked this historical idea first, referring to the prominence and strength associated with Sapta Sindhu in ancient India. He then drew a parallel with the challenges facing the country today.

His argument was that India’s strength was once symbolised by the seven rivers of Sapta Sindhu, while the India of today needs a new set of seven streams through which national strength can flow. That new framework is what he called Saptadhara.

**The seven streams Modi outlined**

1. The first stream is manufacturing, where Modi called for competitiveness across the entire value chain, built on cost, quality and scale, so India becomes a manufacturing base for the world rather than merely a market for it.
2. The second is agriculture and food processing, with an emphasis on chemical-free farming and turning staples such as millets, spices, fruits and vegetables into globally recognised brands rather than raw exports.
3. Technology and innovation forms the third stream. Citing India's success with UPI and digital infrastructure, Modi called for leadership in data centres, robotics and next-generation communications, including indigenously developed 6G.
4. Fourth is Gati Shakti, his connectivity mission covering high-speed rail, highways, waterways, airports and ports, aimed at cutting logistics costs and positioning infrastructure as a competitive economic asset rather than mere construction.
5. The fifth stream is defence self-reliance. Modi pointed to global instability affecting energy, fertiliser and medicine supplies, and pressed for indigenous defence production, including drones and counter-drone systems, with India eventually becoming a global arms supplier.
6. Sixth, he combined the green and blue economies, renewable energy and green hydrogen alongside the maritime potential of India's coastline, fisheries and ocean resources.
7. The seventh and final stream is soft power: yoga, handicrafts, cinema, animation, gaming and tourism, which Modi framed as economic and geopolitical assets in their own right, alongside India's underused wealth of national parks and forests.

# PM Modi unveils seven-pillar 'Sapta Dhara' roadmap for Viksit Bharat

## The framework places manufacturing, food processing and technology at its core, alongside infrastructure, defence, the green and blue economy, and India's soft power

Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the nation during the 8oth Independence Day celebrations, at Red Fort in New Delhi | PTI

Krity Ambey

3 min read  Last Updated : Aug 15 2026 | 11:37 AM IST

#### Listen to This Article

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday outlined a seven-pillar development framework, or “Sapta Dhara”, to guide India’s journey towards becoming a developed economy by 2047, placing manufacturing, food processing and technology at the heart of the next phase of economic growth.

 

In his 80th Independence Day address, Modi said India needed a new growth framework to achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat, identifying seven “streams of strength” that would drive the country’s economic transformation.

 

“The first shakti of the Sapta Dhara is the manufacturing sector. For this, we need to focus on three things—cost, quality, and scale. There should be no compromise with quality. This will be our brand value,” Modi said.

  

The emphasis on manufacturing comes as India seeks to raise the sector’s share in gross domestic product (GDP) to 25 per cent by 2035 from around 17 per cent currently. The government aims to position India as a key alternative production base in global supply chains. Modi’s focus on cost, quality and scale echoes broader efforts to improve export competitiveness and attract investment into manufacturing.

 

The second pillar that the Prime Minister identified for Viksit Bharat was agriculture and food processing. Modi urged industry to leverage the market-access opportunities created by India’s expanding network of free trade agreements (FTAs).

 

“With the new FTAs, we have access to greater global markets now,” he said, advocating a renewed push towards value addition in agriculture and processed food exports.

 

In the current financial year so far, New Delhi has put into effect two trade deals — FTAs with Oman and the United Kingdom (UK). The next on the cards is India’s agreement with the European Union (EU), likely to be signed by December and made effective in the first half of next year.

 

The third pillar highlighted by Modi was technology and innovation, with an emphasis on semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), digital infrastructure and emerging technologies as key drivers of future growth.

 

Beyond these three areas, Modi outlined four additional pillars under the Sapta Dhara framework: Gati Shakti, aimed at strengthening infrastructure and logistics; defence power, centred on self-reliance in arms manufacturing; the green and blue economy, focused on sustainable growth and marine resources; and India’s soft power, encompassing its cultural, diplomatic and global influence.

 

Modi said these seven streams would collectively shape India’s development trajectory as it works towards becoming a developed nation by 2047.

 

The seven-pronged framework reinforces several themes that have featured prominently in recent government policy initiatives, including infrastructure creation, export-led manufacturing, energy transition, technological self-reliance and defence indigenisation.

 

The emphasis on food processing and manufacturing is particularly significant as India seeks to expand its share in global trade while creating large-scale employment opportunities.

 

While the Prime Minister did not announce specific policy measures under the “Sapta Dhara” framework, he said the seven-pillar roadmap would offer a broad blueprint for the government’s economic and development priorities in the coming years.

 

The “Sapta Dhara” can help India achieve in five to seven years what it could not achieve in the past five to seven decades, Modi said.

 

“Through the power of Sapta Dhara, we will give the nation new heights, new momentum, and the ability to outdo new goals,” he said.

# Independence Day 2026: PM Modi unveils ‘Sapta Dhara’ vision, puts youth, self-reliance at core

## The 7 pillars of PM Modi's 2047 vision are manufacturing, farming, technology, Gati Shakti, self-reliance in defence, green economy and soft power — designed to accelerate national growth over the next decade and more

##### Ajay Banerjee

##### Tribune News Service

New Delhi, Updated At : 05:36 PM Aug 15, 2026 IST

Follow us  Connect with us

Prime Minister Narendra Modi meets students during the 80th Independence Day celebrations, at Red Fort in New Delhi. (PMO via PTI Photo)

Advertisement

Charting an ambitious blueprint to transform the country into a developed nation by 2047, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, delivering his customary Independence Day speech from the ramparts of the Red Fort, unveiled a ‘Sapta Dhara’ vision, or a seven-pillar framework.

Advertisement

The seven pillars are manufacturing, farming, technology, Gati Shakti, self-reliance in defence, the green economy and soft power—designed to accelerate national growth over the next decade and beyond.

Advertisement

Less than a month after massive protests by youth at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, Modi focused on the younger generation and promised that 1 crore young people would be trained in AI over the next year through a nationwide mission-mode initiative.

Advertisement

Advertisement

He added that free online coaching will be provided to youth preparing for various competitive examinations and for sports. A nationwide campaign will target children aged between 5 and 15 years across villages and cities.

Amid evolving global supply chain dynamics, PM Modi positioned energy independence as an urgent national priority. He noted that domestic piped natural gas (PNG) networks have expanded from 70 cities 12 years ago to more than 700 cities today, connecting 1.75 crore households.

On nuclear energy, Modi set a target of 100 GW of capacity by 2047 and added that five new reactors would become operational within the next 6–7 years. “Nuclear energy is a major means of energy security. We have paved the way towards a new goal by passing the ‘Shanti Act’ in Parliament.”

This year, India achieved a significant milestone by mastering fast-breeder nuclear technology, marking a major stride towards self-reliance in nuclear fuel, Modi said.

Modi urged the nation to broaden its thinking. “A nation is rarely held back by a lack of resources; rather, it is often constrained by the limitations of its mindset. When thinking stagnates and becomes confined by boundaries, we fail to recognise our own true potential,” Modi said.

Modi said the country remains dependent on crude oil, a situation stemming from a flawed mindset. He cited how 99% of the nation’s coastline had been designated as a no-go area.

“We had effectively decided against exploring the ocean depths. That was a poverty of thought. The government decided this could not continue. We have opened up 99% of the areas that were once ‘no-go zones’ as ‘go-ahead zones’. We are now actively engaged in deep-sea exploration and the search for new reserves.”

Last year’s “Samudra Manthan” project was a significant step in this direction, Modi said, adding that Rs 85,000 crore had been allocated for the purpose.

On the manufacturing sector, Modi said the country needs to focus on three things: cost, quality and scale. “There should be no compromise on quality. This will be our brand value.” He cited recent free trade agreements with other countries, adding that food processing would gain access to wider global markets.

Touching upon technology, innovation and digital technologies, Modi called for deeper domestic manufacturing capabilities across critical technology and defence sectors.

Modi said India was moving towards self-reliance in semiconductor manufacturing as chips become increasingly important for electronic goods, medical equipment and transportation systems.

He said three major semiconductor plants had already started operations and their production was expected to be exported. The Prime Minister also said another five to eight semiconductor plants were likely to become operational over the next seven to eight years.

The Prime Minister linked the expansion of semiconductor manufacturing to India’s Atmanirbhar Bharat push and the goal of becoming a Viksit Bharat by 2047.

Critical minerals also featured prominently in the self-reliance pitch, as Modi mentioned the need to secure access to resources crucial for the country’s future energy, industrial and technological requirements.

India has been stepping up efforts to reduce its dependence on imported critical minerals through the National Critical Minerals Mission. These minerals are important for sectors including clean energy, high-tech manufacturing and defence.

The push has assumed greater importance as India seeks to expand domestic manufacturing in areas such as semiconductors, renewable energy and electric mobility, all of which depend on secure supplies of strategic raw materials.

Modi went on to announce that the country would establish a vibrant Civil Defence network in the coming days.

“Measures need to be put in place to protect citizens from modern-day crises. We are going to create a massive, modern Civil Defence volunteer force capable of overcoming contemporary challenges,” Modi said.

On internal security, Modi said that for years, individuals with a Maoist mindset had entrenched themselves within the corridors of power in the country.

“This Maoist ideology influenced policies, even through their roles as advisors on government committees. We have succeeded in eliminating armed Naxals in the forests and freeing the nation from that crisis. However, while the armed Naxals are gone, ‘Dimagi Naxals’ remain, and those who harbour this mindset are waiting for an opportunity. We must identify these ‘Dimagi Naxals’. We need to isolate them and align the nation’s youth with the mainstream effort to transform the country into a developed nation.”

On self-reliance, Modi said every nation had shifted towards a mindset of looking after its own interests. Unfortunately, during this period of crisis, some have played the game of weaponising resources to assert their dominance. The world is busy weaponising whatever it possesses—be it petrol, diesel, fertilisers, medicines or technology chips.

He highlighted India’s journey over the last 12 years from one of the “Fragile Five” economies to the world’s fastest-growing major economy.

“By 2014, we had become a part of the ‘Fragile Five’. But in the last 12 years, we picked up pace,” PM Modi told the gathering.

Prime Minister Modi concluded his 13th Red Fort address by expressing solidarity with regions affected by recent seasonal monsoon floods and landslides, promising full national support for recovery efforts.

## Decoding ‘Sapta Dhara’

**Manufacturing power:** Build complete domestic end-to-end value chains, from design to components, focusing on zero-defect quality, cost and global scale.

**Agriculture and food processing:** Create integrated farm-to-export supply chains for millets, spices and fruits while transitioning to chemical-free farming.

**Technology and innovation:** Evolve from a tech market into a global innovation hub leading in AI, quantum technology, space, robotics, DPI and Made-in-India 6G.

**Gati Shakti:** Establish high-speed, seamless multimodal logistics connecting cities, highways, railways, airports and modern industrial seaports.

**Defence Shakti:** Achieve complete strategic self-reliance by pioneering and exporting next-generation defence technologies such as drones, counter-drone systems and hypersonics.

**Green and blue economy:** Scale sustainable growth through green hydrogen, renewables and energy storage, alongside the full utilisation of ocean, coastal and marine potential.

**India’s soft power:** Globalise Indian culture, yoga, Ayurveda and tourism while establishing global leadership in gaming, VFX, animation and the creative economy.

# PM Modi outlines ‘Sapta Dhara’ roadmap, sets 2047 deadline for Viksit Bharat

* Nation

Photo: x.com/PMOIndia

India Verve Desk

* August 15, 2026

* 3 mins read

New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, addressing the nation from the Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, on Saturday unveiled a seven-point strategy, termed “Sapta Dhara,” to guide India towards becoming a developed nation by 2047.

The PM said Vande Mataram was sung at the Red Fort for the first time since independence, coinciding with the song’s 150th anniversary, and paid tribute to freedom fighters including Mahatma Gandhi.

He said around 25 crore Indians had moved out of poverty over the past 12 years, and that India had grown from being labelled among the “Fragile Five” economies in 2014 to the fastest-growing major economy today.

He cited a near fourfold rise in defence production, a sevenfold increase in electronics manufacturing, and a 100-fold jump in digital transactions over the period, according to an official statement.

Reiterating the government’s push for self-reliance, the PM said three semiconductor plants were now operational and exporting, with five to eight more expected in the coming years. He said India aimed to achieve 100 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity by 2047, alongside expanded solar capacity and gas pipeline coverage. He also referred to India’s first hydrogen-powered train and full electrification of the railway network.

He said India had withstood recent global disruptions, including the pandemic and conflicts abroad, without shortages of fuel or fertiliser, and cautioned against the “weaponisation” of global resources by some nations. He urged MSMEs to leverage nearly 40 free trade agreements signed since 2014 to expand exports in textiles, pharmaceuticals and seafood.

Outlining the seven pillars of his roadmap, the PM listed:

a) Manufacturing power – building a complete domestic value chain with a focus on quality and zero-defect production  
b) Agriculture and food processing – promoting chemical-free farming and global branding of Indian produce  
c) Technology and innovation – strengthening digital infrastructure and pursuing leadership in AI, 6G and quantum computing  
d) Connectivity – expanding high-speed rail, highways and port-led development  
e) Defence – self-reliance in production, and leadership in drone and hypersonic technology  
f) Green and blue economy – renewable energy, green hydrogen and coastal economic development  
g) Soft power – leveraging yoga, tourism, cinema and creative industries globally

He also announced that one crore youth would be trained in AI skills over the next year, and said a nationwide talent hunt would identify sporting talent among children aged 5 to 15 ahead of India’s bid for the 2036 Olympics and its hosting of the 2030 Commonwealth Games.

On security, Modi said Naxal violence had nearly been eliminated after decades of conflict and announced a modern civil defence network to prepare citizens against evolving threats.

He highlighted the growing role of women in the armed forces and STEM fields, said the Lakhpati Didi scheme had crossed its 3-crore target with a new goal of 6 crore set, and renewed his appeal to political parties to implement women’s reservation in legislatures.

He said the Ayushman Bharat scheme had extended health coverage to 100 crore citizens, up from 25 crore before 2014, and urged citizens to actively participate in the ongoing Census by submitting accurate details digitally.

Modi closed his address by calling on citizens to place national interest above self-interest in pursuit of a developed India by 2047.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address from the Red Fort, outlined ‘Shakti Ki Saptadhara’, a seven-point framework that he said would strengthen India’s self-reliance and support its next phase of economic development.

The first pillar is manufacturing, with Modi calling for globally competitive costs, quality and scale and greater participation in global supply chains.

Agriculture and food processing form the second stream. Modi said India must turn farm produce, including millets, spices, fruits and vegetables, into globally recognised brands and connect farmers more directly with export markets.

The third pillar, technology and innovation, focuses on areas including data centres, robotics and next-generation communications. Modi highlighted UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure as examples of India’s capabilities and called for Made-in-India 6G technology to expand across the country.

Gati Shakti, the fourth stream, will focus on faster and seamless connectivity through roads, expressways and other infrastructure to support economic activity.

The fifth pillar, Raksha Shakti, centres on self-reliance in defence manufacturing, with particular attention to drone and counter-drone technologies.

Modi identified green energy as the sixth stream, calling for greater innovation and investment to tap India’s potential in the sector.

The seventh pillar is soft power, covering areas such as Yoga, handicrafts, films, animation, gaming, digital content and tourism. Modi also highlighted India’s national parks and other attractions as opportunities to expand international tourism.

Together, the seven areas form the framework Modi presented as key to building a more self-reliant and developed India.

title: PM Modi outlines seven growth streams in ‘Shakti Ki Saptadhara’
content:
ANI Photo | PM Modi defines seven streams of growth in ‘Shakti Ki Saptadhara’ on Independence Day

Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled ‘Shakti Ki Saptadhara’ during his address on August 15, outlining seven pillars that constitute India’s strengths and will power the nation’s future development.

Speaking from the Red Fort, PM Modi stated that these seven streams would guide India’s path to becoming a developed nation, Viksit Bharat. He emphasised the need to significantly expand manufacturing, describing it as central to India’s economic growth.

“From Design to Manufacturing, India must become a reliable hub in the global supply chain. For this, I want to place special emphasis on 3 things. My brothers and sisters in the field of Manufacturing, do not let this opportunity slip away. For this, we will have to meet global standards on cost, quality, and scale,” he said.

The Prime Minister identified agriculture and food processing as the second strength. He highlighted the opportunities arising from free trade agreements (FTAs) that open vast global markets for Indian farmers. “We must go from the farm to the export market. Our traditional cuisine, millets, spices, and fruits and flowers should become global brands,” he added.

The third pillar is technology and innovation. PM Modi highlighted India’s emerging technologies, stating, “Today is the era of AI, quantum, space, robotics, and data centres. Emerging technology is also challenging us every moment. We need to become a hub of innovation. We have proven our mettle in UPI and digital public infrastructure. Now India has to take digital public technologies to every corner of the world. India has to lead in Next Generation Communication Technology. Made in India 6G should reach every corner–this should be our goal.”

The fourth pillar, Gati Shakti, focuses on seamless, high-speed connectivity, including high-speed rail, modern highways, inland waterways, airports, multi-modal logistics hubs, ports, and port-led development.

Defence production is the fifth strength. PM Modi stressed the importance of self-reliance, saying, “It is essential to be self-reliant in the defence sector; this has now been experienced by both India and the world. When the world is immersed in its own thoughts, India cannot remain merely a market for the world. We must become self-reliant in the field of defence. By developing Next Generation Defence Technology, we must move forward in the direction of becoming a global supplier.”

The sixth strength is green energy. PM Modi called for innovation and global leadership in green hydrogen, renewable energy, and energy storage. He also highlighted the potential of the Blue Economy in fisheries, coastal tourism, and ocean technology as new avenues for growth.

India’s soft power forms the seventh stream. The Prime Minister cited Yoga, Ayurveda, handicrafts, culture, films, animation, gaming, digital content, and the creative sector as key assets. He remarked, “Today, Yoga has connected the world to India. Our Ayurveda, holistic healthcare, handicrafts, culture, films, animation, gaming, digital content. The world is recognising and looking forward to India’s WAVES summit. We have more than 100 national parks. We have an opportunity to attract foreign tourists through the power of soft power.”

The Independence Day ceremony included the hoisting of the National Flag at the Red Fort by PM Modi, synchronised with a 21-Gun Salute by the 1721 Field Battery (Ceremonial). The ceremonial battery, commanded by Major Pawan Singh Shekhawat and with Naib Subedar Anuthosh Sarkar as the Gun Position Officer, used indigenous 105mm Light Field Guns.

**# Baljit Balli, Editor

##**

  + PM Modi unveils 'Shakti Ki Saptadhara', defines seven streams to power Viksit Bharat

    Babushahi Network

    New Delhi, August 15, 2026 (ANI): Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday unveiled 'Shakti Ki Saptadhara' in his 80th Independence Day address, defining seven streams that are India's strength and will power India's next level of growth.  
    Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort, PM Modi said these seven pillars would shape India's journey to Viksit Bharat.  
    Calling for a major expansion of manufacturing, the Prime Minister described it as the key driver of India's future economic growth.  
    "From Design to Manufacturing, India must become a reliable hub in the global supply chain. For this, I want to place special emphasis on 3 things. My brothers and sisters in the field of Manufacturing, do not let this opportunity slip away. For this, we will have to meet global standards on cost, quality, and scale," PM Modi said.  
    The Prime Minister said the second strength is agriculture and food processing.  
    "The second strength of Saptadhara is agriculture and food processing. We must move forward in this direction. The world's markets are now open for our farmers. Due to FTAs, we are gaining access to a very large market; we must reach it. We must go from the farm to the export market. Our traditional cuisine, millets, spices, and fruits and flowers should become global brands.The second strength of this Saptadhara is agriculture and food production. Today, global markets are opening up, and through FTAs, we are gaining access to vast new markets. Whether it is our spices or millets, they must become global brands," he said.  
    He described the third strength as Technology and Innovation.  
    "Today is the era of AI, quantum, space, robotics, and data centers. Emerging technology is also challenging us every moment. We need to become a hub of innovation. We have proven our mettle in UPI and digital public infrastructure. Now India has to take digital public technologies to every corner of the world. India has to lead in Next Generation Communication Technology. Made in India 6G should reach every corner--this should be our goal. This is the era of robotics, AI, quantum technology, space and data centres. Emerging technologies are presenting new challenges, and we must become a global hub of innovation. We have already demonstrated our strength through UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure. Now, we must take the next leap in next-generation communication technology.  
    On the fourth pillar, PM Modi said Gati Shakti must focus on "seamless and high speed connectivity. Our cities must be connected through high speed rail. We must also focus on port-led development."  
    "We need seamless high-speed rail connectivity, modern highway connectivity, inland waterways, airports, multi-modal logistics hubs and ports. We have to work towards port-led development. The fifth 'shakti' is Defence production, in which we must become self-reliant and aim to become a global supplier," PM Modi added on his speech.  
    PM Modi said defence is the fifth strength of 'Saptdhara'. He added that India has to work towards defence manufacturing and Atmanirbhar defence.  
    It is essential to be self-reliant in the defence sector; this has now been experienced by both India and the world. When the world is immersed in its own thoughts, India cannot remain merely a market for the world. We must become self-reliant in the field of defence. By developing Next Generation Defence Technology, we must move forward in the direction of becoming a global supplier.  
    Describing green energy as the sixth strength of Saptadhara, the Prime Minister called for greater innovation in the sector.  
    "India must achieve global leadership in green hydrogen, renewable energy and energy storage, while continuing to provide solutions to global challenges. The Blue Economy, too, offers immense opportunities in fisheries, coastal tourism and ocean technology, opening new pathways for India's growth," he said.  
    PM Modi added, "We must work in the areas of renewable energy, energy storage, green storage and manufacturing. India has an opportunity in the area of the Blue Economy."  
    PM Modi said India's 'soft power' is the seventh strength of Saptadhara, highlighting Yoga, handicrafts, films, animation, gaming, digital content and the broader creative sector as key strengths.  
    "Today, Yoga has connected the world to India. Our Ayurveda, holistic healthcare, handicrafts, culture, films, animation, gaming, digital content. The world is recognizing and looking forward to India's WAVES summit. We have more than 100 national parks. We have an opportunity to attract foreign tourists through the power of soft power," he said.  
    PM Modi hoisted the National Flag at the Red Fort. The flag hoisting was synchronised with a 21-Gun Salute by the gunners of the 1721 Field Battery (Ceremonial).  
    The ceremonial battery used indigenous 105mm Light Field Guns and was commanded by Major Pawan Singh Shekhawat, while Naib Subedar (Assistant Instructor in Gunnery) Anuthosh Sarkar served as the Gun Position Officer. (ANI)

title: What is Sapta Dhara? PM Modi Announces 7 Pillars to Achieve Viksit Bharat by 2047
content:
# What is Sapta Dhara? PM Modi Announces 7 Pillars to Achieve Viksit Bharat by 2047

By Manisha Waldia

**Last Updated:** Aug 15, 2026, 15:32 IST

## What is Sapta Dhara? Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled the 7-pillar Sapta Dhara framework during his Independence Day speech in 2026, a roadmap to achieve the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.

What is Sapta Dhara? PM Modi Announces 7 Pillars to Achieve Viksit Bharat by 2047

The Prime Minister Narendra Modi revealed the Sapta Dhara framework during his speech on Independence Day 2026 at the Red Fort. It consists of seven components that will help India become a Viksit Bharat (developed country) by the year 2047. This initiative aims to prompt economic progress, enact reforms in governance, stimulate new innovations, provide more social security and establish the country as a major player in the world economy.

The framework was presented as the country celebrates a huge milestone on its way to development and looks towards the Independence Day celebrations in 2047. 

## Sapta Dhara: 7 Pillars for Viksit Bharat by 2047

The objective of the Sapta Dhara initiative is to mobilize resources and implement projects in seven identified areas to boost inclusive, sustainable and future-oriented growth.

### 1. Manufacturing Sector

The first area involves promoting India as a leading provider of global supply chain solutions. PM Modi has put forward three essentials for Indian industry and MSMEs: affordability, quality, and scale. 

The objective is to achieve end-to-end value chains from concept to zero-defect manufacturing, establishing world-class brand recognition for Indian-made products.

### 2. Agriculture Sector

The second area seeks to transform Indian agriculture into an international business by capitalizing on recently completed Free Trade Agreements (FTAs). Food processing, value addition, and exports will be brought to scale in line with international demand.

### 3. Technology and Innovation

The third component focuses on a technology and industry base ready for the future. It focuses on advancing domestic technology and industry in areas such as semiconductor manufacturing, AI (with a definite plan to train 1 crore individuals in AI), robotics, quantum technology, outer space and advanced telecommunication systems.

### 4. Gati Shakti (Infrastructure & Logistics)

The fourth component is built upon the integrated logistics plan of India. The primary objective is an integrated transport system with efficient connectivity of major urban centers using high-speed trains and port-based growth.

### 5. Defence Power (Raksha Shakti)

The fifth component aims for self-sufficiency in defence equipment manufacturing. PM Modi underlined that India should transition from the biggest defence import country to a leading global defence exporter, taking a leadership position in advanced technologies like hypersonic technology.

### 6. Green and Blue Economy

The sixth pillar is all about combining environmental sustainability and coastal development. The vision is to become a leader in green hydrogen and renewable energy storage and have a total of 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047. At the same time, the blue economy utilizes India’s vast coastline for sustainable fisheries, ocean technology, and coastal tourism.

## 7. Soft Power

The last stream aims to enhance India’s cultural presence around the world. This involves promoting Yoga, Ayurveda, and holistic medicine under the "Heal in India" initiative and its creative industries, such as handicrafts, cinema, VFX, gaming, and digital content creation.

## Why Sapta Dhara Matters for India’s Future?

It is necessary to dismantle traditional bureaucratic silos to achieve the status of a developed country by 2047. By organizing our progress into seven interrelated streams, decisions made in one area, for example in technology or green energy, will always boost our performance in manufacturing, agriculture, and defense industries. 

PM Modi stated that the implementation of all seven streams in the next five to seven years will give the necessary momentum to a process that otherwise requires decades. Thus speeding up the movement of India to Viksit Bharat.
