title: PM Modi lays out 'Sapta Dhara' roadmap for Viksit Bharat 2047, announces 1 crore AI-skilled youth and major reforms - DD India
content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday called for a faster pace of reforms, greater self-reliance and a renewed national effort to build a “Viksit Bharat” by 2047, unveiling a seven-point development framework centred on manufacturing, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, the green and blue economy, and India’s soft power.

Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said India could no longer afford “small dreams” and urged citizens to combine ambitious goals with firm resolve and greater national capabilities.

“Bharat has also set a very big dream today – a dream backed by firm resolve, a dream of reaching new heights. And that dream is this: when we complete 100 years of independence in 2047, we will have built a ‘Viksit Bharat’,” he said.

The Prime Minister said the goal would have to be achieved through the collective efforts of 140 crore citizens and asserted that the determination of the world’s most populous country to become a developed nation would change the way the world views India.

‘Vande Mataram’ echoes from Red Fort for first time since Independence

Beginning his address, PM Modi greeted the nation on the 80th Independence Day and paid tribute to freedom fighters, revolutionaries and Mahatma Gandhi.

“Today, every heartbeat resonates with the chant of Vande Mataram. Today, there is ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Hai, Har Man Tiranga Hai’,” he said.

He described the occasion as historic as “for the first time since independence, Vande Mataram is echoing from the Red Fort on August 15”, coinciding with the commemoration of 150 years of the national song.

PM Modi also expressed solidarity with people affected by floods and landslides in several parts of the country.

“I want to assure the affected families that we and the entire nation stand firmly with them,” he said.

‘We can no longer move forward with small dreams’

The Prime Minister said India’s development journey required larger ambitions, stronger resolutions and greater capabilities.

“We can no longer move forward with small dreams. We must dream big, because big dreams expand our thinking,” PM Modi said.

He said strong resolve enables a nation to overcome difficulties and challenges, while high ambitions raise the scale of its capabilities and efforts.

PM Modi highlighted India’s economic and social progress over the past 12 years, saying 25 crore people had moved out of poverty and the country had progressed from being counted among the “Fragile Five” to becoming a major and the fastest-growing major economy.

He said the achievements were the result of the collective efforts of people across social and geographical groups.

“Over the past 12 years, crores of citizens of the country… have made every possible effort to take the nation to new heights with determination and dedication,” he said.

Defence production up nearly four-fold, mobile manufacturing 35 times

Listing India’s progress, PM Modi said defence production had increased nearly four-fold, Khadi and Village Industries production nearly five-fold and electronics manufacturing nearly seven-fold over the past 12 years.

Production of modern railway coaches, he said, had increased 21 times and mobile phone production 35 times.

He also pointed to a nearly four-fold increase in internet users and patents granted, while digital transactions had increased 100 times.

The pace of providing tap-water connections, gas connections, toilets and houses to the poor had also increased substantially, he said.

PM Modi said thousands of compliances had been eliminated and hundreds of outdated laws repealed.

“The march of the 21st century cannot be carried out using the laws of the previous century,” he said.

‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ central to development strategy

The Prime Minister stressed that self-confidence and self-reliance were essential for India to become a developed country.

“Bharat should no longer live by depending on other countries. We must become self-reliant,” he said.

He said India was moving forward with Make in India, Swadeshi and Vocal for Local and argued that reliance on imported products, even when cheaper, did not build domestic capabilities.

India expanding semiconductor manufacturing

PM Modi cited semiconductors as an example of India’s drive towards technological self-reliance.

He said three major semiconductor plants had already started and that production had begun to be exported.

“Over the coming seven to eight years, another five, seven, or even eight semiconductor plants are expected to begin operations very soon,” he said.

He also highlighted the National Critical Minerals Mission and the government’s efforts to secure access to critical minerals, which he said were essential for the technology sector.

Nuclear power target of 100 GW by 2047

Energy security, PM Modi said, would be increasingly important as India expands AI, data centres, semiconductors and other energy-intensive technologies.

“Energy security is the need of the hour,” he said, highlighting nuclear power as a major component of the strategy.

He said the passage of the SHANTI Act had opened a new path and that India was working towards a target of 100 GW of nuclear power by 2047.

“Within this very decade, we have set a target of starting five new nuclear reactors,” he said.

PM Modi also said India had crossed an important milestone by mastering fast breeder nuclear technology, describing it as a major step towards self-reliance in nuclear fuel.

₹85,000 crore allocation for ‘Samudra Manthan’

The Prime Minister said India had historically restricted exploration of much of its coastal area, describing the approach as a “poverty of thought”.

He said 99% of India’s coastal area that had earlier been designated as a “No-Go Area” had now been opened for exploration.

“We have opened up that 99%, which was once designated as a No-Go Area, as a Go-Ahead Area, and we are now moving towards exploring the sea and discovering new reserves,” he said.

PM Modi said the government had recently decided to allocate ₹85,000 crore to accelerate the “Samudra Manthan” initiative.

Solar capacity rises from 2 GW to 160 GW

Highlighting India’s transition towards cleaner energy, PM Modi said piped gas infrastructure had expanded from 70 cities in 2014 to 700 cities.

The number of households covered by piped gas, he said, had risen from around 20-22 lakh to nearly 1.75 crore.

Solar energy capacity had also grown from just 2 GW before 2014 to 160 GW, he said.

He highlighted the progress under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, saying solar systems had been installed in 50 lakh homes.

“The electricity bills of thousands of households have become zero, while thousands of households are now earning by selling the surplus electricity they generate,” PM Modi said.

India completes railway electrification

PM Modi highlighted the rapid electrification of India’s railway network, saying only 30% of the network had been electrified in the 90 years after work began in 1925.

“We completed 100% of the work within this one decade. 30% in 90 years, 70% in 10 years – this is what work looks like,” he said.

He said railway electrification had reduced India’s dependence on imported diesel while also benefiting the environment.

PM Modi also highlighted India’s entry into hydrogen-powered rail transport.

“The country has started its first hydrogen-powered train, and I am pleased that it is the longest and most powerful train of its kind,” he said.

India needs to seize opportunities created by FTAs

The Prime Minister said India had entered into Free Trade Agreements with nearly 40 countries since 2014 and urged businesses, particularly MSMEs, to take advantage of expanded global market access.

“These trade agreements that have been made are a huge opportunity and hence I would especially like to tell my MSMEs that we should not miss this opportunity,” he said.

He called for Indian textiles, machinery, medicines, seafood and other products to reach global markets while meeting international standards on quality and cost.

“Our textile sector, spanning from Ludhiana in Punjab to Tiruppur in Tamil Nadu, has the potential to reach global markets,” he said.

He also pointed to the potential for Indian seafood exports, particularly shrimp, to expand through greater access to international markets.

‘Sapta Dhara’ to drive India’s next phase of development

The central theme of PM Modi’s address was the ‘Sapta Dhara’, or seven streams of national power, which he presented as the framework for India’s development over the next phase.

“The first power of Sapta Dhara is – manufacturing power,” he said.

The seven areas identified by the Prime Minister are:

1. Manufacturing power  
2. Agriculture and food production  
3. Technology and innovation  
4. Gati Shakti  
5. Raksha Shakti  
6. Green economy and blue economy  
7. India’s soft power

On manufacturing, PM Modi called for India to build complete value chains, from components to finished products and from design to manufacturing.

“India must emerge as a trusted hub in the global supply chain,” he said.

He identified cost, quality and scale as three key requirements and stressed the need for “zero-defect precision manufacturing”.

“Our mantra should be quality, quality, quality,” he said.

Farmers urged to move from farm to export market

Agriculture was identified as the second stream of Sapta Dhara.

PM Modi called for greater emphasis on food processing and exports, saying Indian farmers now had access to larger global markets through FTAs.

“We have to move from the farm to the export market,” he said.

He highlighted India’s traditional foods, millets, spices, fruits and flowers as products capable of becoming global brands and urged greater adoption of chemical-free farming.

‘Made-in-India 6G should reach every corner of the world’

Technology and innovation constituted the third pillar of the framework.

PM Modi said India must not merely become a market for global technology companies but should emerge as an innovation hub.

“Today is the age of AI, quantum technology, space, robotics and data centres. An entirely new domain has opened up,” he said.

He highlighted India’s experience with UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure and called for Indian digital technologies to be taken to the world.

“Bharat must lead in next-generation communication technologies. Our goal should be to ensure that Made-in-India 6G reaches every corner of the world,” he said.

Gati Shakti to focus on seamless connectivity

The fourth stream, Gati Shakti, would focus on faster and seamless connectivity through high-speed rail, highways, inland waterways, airports and multimodal logistics.

PM Modi called for a shift towards port-led development, saying ports should be seen not merely as locations for loading and unloading cargo but as engines of economic growth.

Defence self-reliance and next-generation technologies

Under the fifth stream, Raksha Shakti, PM Modi stressed the importance of self-reliance in defence.

“There is no alternative to being self-reliant in defence,” he said.

He called for India to develop next-generation defence technologies, drones, counter-drone systems and hypersonic defence capabilities and emerge as a global defence supplier.

He also highlighted cybersecurity as a growing area of national security where India’s youth could contribute.

Green and blue economy to create new jobs

The sixth stream will focus on the green and blue economy.

PM Modi called for India to achieve global scale in green hydrogen, renewable energy, energy storage, green mobility and green manufacturing.

He also highlighted the potential of India’s coastline for fisheries, coastal tourism and ocean technology.

“Bharat also has enormous opportunities in the blue economy,” he said.

Yoga, Ayurveda, culture and entertainment as India’s soft power

The seventh stream is India’s soft power.

PM Modi highlighted yoga, Ayurveda, faith, holistic healthcare, handicrafts, culture, films, VFX, animation, gaming and digital content as areas through which India could expand its global influence.

He called for the Heal in India initiative and the WAVES Summit to be used to showcase India’s capabilities.

The Prime Minister also highlighted India’s tourism potential, saying the country could attract more international visitors through its cultural and natural heritage.

“Why shouldn’t major global sporting events be held in Bharat?” he asked, also pointing to the growing concert economy and opportunities to build India as a global destination for entertainment.

PM Modi sets ambitious target for Indian companies

Calling for a stronger global presence for Indian businesses, PM Modi asked why 50 of the Fortune 500 companies could not be based in India within the next decade.

“Why shouldn’t an Indian bank’s flag fly among the world’s top banks? We should have an Indian bank among the world’s top five banks,” he said.

He similarly called for Indian pharmaceutical companies, consulting firms, accounting firms and technology companies to achieve global leadership.

“Our brands should become an identity of our country and make Bharat a destination for the world,” PM Modi said.

‘Reform Express’ to accelerate in coming years

PM Modi said India needed to change its work culture, thinking and pace of execution to achieve the 2047 goal.

“The work which has not been done in the last 5-7 decades, we have to do that work in the coming 5-7 years,” he said.

He described reforms not as a compulsion or a buzzword but as a matter of conviction.

“We have embarked on the ‘Reform Express’ and we are going to move towards next level reform in the coming days as well,” PM Modi said.

He called for the Centre, states, local governments, industry, producers and farmers to reform traditional systems and approaches.

One crore youth to be trained in AI skills

A major announcement in the address was the decision to train one crore young Indians in AI skills within the next year.

“We have decided that, in the next one year, we will train one crore young people in AI skills, so that the youth of our country have the capability to lead in the world of AI as well,” PM Modi said.

He also highlighted more than 2.5 lakh registered startups, the ₹1 lakh crore Innovation Fund, Skill India, the National Drone Policy, Khelo India and the opening up of India’s space sector.

Bioeconomy grows from ₹60,000 crore to ₹20 lakh crore

PM Modi highlighted the expansion of India’s bioeconomy, saying its turnover had risen from ₹60,000 crore before 2014 to ₹20 lakh crore.

He also said electric vehicle sales had increased from 1.5 lakh units in 2009-10 to 25 lakh units in 2025-26.

The aviation sector, Made-in-India aircraft production and drone-based applications were also highlighted as emerging areas of opportunity for young Indians.

Free online coaching for competitive examinations

Addressing concerns of middle-class families over the rising cost of coaching, PM Modi announced a programme to provide free online coaching for young people preparing for various examinations.

“The pressure of coaching classes has become a major burden for our middle-class families,” he said.

“We have the digital public infrastructure, we have excellent talent and we have teachers. By bringing these resources together, we are going to build an extensive network to provide free coaching to the young people of the country,” he added.

India steps up preparations for 2036 Olympics

PM Modi said India was moving towards becoming a strong contender to host the 2036 Olympic Games and highlighted the country’s preparations to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030.

He said India needed to expand participation in sporting disciplines in which it currently had little or no representation.

“We want the 2036 Olympics to be held in Bharat,” he said.

He announced a talent-hunt campaign across villages, cities and schools to identify children aged between five and 15 with sporting potential and provide them specialised training.

100-week campaign for ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat’

The Prime Minister also called for a collective campaign against drug abuse.

He said volunteers of My Bharat, NGOs, social and cultural organisations and spiritual leaders had come together to launch a 100-week programme for a Drugs-Free India.

“A ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat’ or Drugs-Free India must be a collective responsibility for all of us,” PM Modi said.

Naxalism nearly eliminated, PM Modi warns against ‘mental Naxals’

PM Modi said the government had made a determined effort since 2014 to eliminate Naxalism and Maoist violence.

“Naxalite-Maoist violence may no longer even have the strength to take its final breath. We are moving towards eliminating it completely,” he said.

He said areas once affected by violence were now witnessing development and the flying of the Tricolour.

However, he warned against what he termed “mental Naxals”, whom he accused of seeking opportunities to promote violence and anarchy.

“We must identify these mental Naxals, isolate them, and steer the nation’s youth toward the mainstream effort of transforming India into a developed nation,” he said.

‘Mission Sudarshan Chakra’ and modern civil defence network

On national security, PM Modi said India needed to prepare for changing forms of warfare, where critical infrastructure such as refineries, banks and data centres could be targeted.

He said work on Mission Sudarshan Chakra was progressing rapidly.

India’s defence exports, he said, had increased nearly 50 times and Indian weapons were reaching about 100 countries.

The Prime Minister also announced plans to establish a modern civil defence network.

“The civil defence systems that have developed in our country in accordance with the wars of the last century have become outdated,” he said.

“We are going to create a huge voluntary force of civil defence to overcome modern challenges,” he added.

6 crore ‘Lakhpati Didis’ target

PM Modi highlighted the growing role of women in India’s development, including in aviation, fighter jets, sports, STEM education, the armed forces and semiconductor manufacturing.

He said the government had already surpassed its target of creating three crore Lakhpati Didis and was now working towards creating six crore Lakhpati Didis.

“The creation of 3 crore new Lakhpati Didis signifies a massive transformation in the rural economy driven by the power of women,” he said.

Appeal for 33% representation for women

The Prime Minister appealed to political parties to implement women’s reservation in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies at the earliest.

“Let us step forward to uphold their dignity and ensure that our mothers and sisters secure 33% representation in the Legislative Assemblies and the Lok Sabha as soon as possible,” he said.

He urged all political parties to support the cause of women’s representation.

Social security coverage expanded to 100 crore

PM Modi said social security coverage had expanded significantly, from 25 crore people before 2014 to 100 crore people within a decade.

He also highlighted the Ayushman Bharat scheme, under which people aged above 70 are eligible for free healthcare coverage of up to ₹5 lakh.

He said the scheme had saved families around ₹2 lakh crore that would otherwise have been spent on medicines and medical procedures.

PM Modi urges youth to participate in Census

The Prime Minister appealed to young people to help their families complete the census exercise accurately using digital technology.

He said accurate census information was essential for policymaking and national planning.

“Counting is not just about figures. Policies are made from its details, plans are made, the country prepares its roadmap for moving forward and hence it is very important to have accurate information,” he said.

He urged families to carefully check information and use the digital process to reduce errors.

‘Panch Pran’ and call for national unity

Towards the conclusion of his address, PM Modi recalled the Panch Pran he had earlier articulated from the Red Fort and called for continued efforts to eliminate the mentality of slavery and strengthen national pride.

He invoked the legacy of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, B.R. Ambedkar, Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru, Syama Prasad Mookerjee, Birsa Munda and Jyotiba Phule.

“The nation’s interest must come before our own, and duty must define our identity,” he said.

“This is our time, this is our moment, and this is our resolve. Let us transform dreams into resolve, resolve into capability, and capability into success,” PM Modi said.

He concluded with a call for collective national effort to build a developed India.

“Let us together build a developed India,” he said before leading the nation in chants of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai” and “Vande Mataram.”

# PM Modi’s ‘Saptadhara’ Explained: 7 Pillars That Will Shape India’s Journey to Viksit Bharat 2047

## PM Modi’s Saptadhara vision outlines seven pillars for Viksit Bharat 2047, manufacturing, farmers, technology, infrastructure, defence, green energy and soft power to drive India’s future growth.

Post Published By: Sreeja Chowdhury

Updated : 15 August 2026, 9:12 AM IST

Prime Minister Narendra Modi (Img: X)

Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 80th Independence Day address from the Red Fort outlined a roadmap for India’s journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047. At the centre of this vision is Saptadhara's seven key pillars that represent India’s growth potential, self-reliance and global aspirations.

The seven pillars cover major areas including manufacturing, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, green energy and India’s cultural influence. PM Modi said these streams of strength can help India become more competitive, innovative and self-reliant on the global stage.

## 1. Manufacturing: Building India as a Global Production Hub

Manufacturing is the first pillar of Saptadhara. PM Modi stressed the need for India to expand its manufacturing ecosystem and become an important part of global supply chains.

He highlighted the importance of producing not just finished products but also critical components within the country. The focus, he said, should be on improving quality, reducing costs and achieving global-scale production.

## 2. Kisan Shakti: Strengthening Agriculture and Food Security

The second pillar focuses on India’s farmers and agricultural sector. PM Modi described agriculture as a key driver of India’s future growth.

The vision aims to strengthen the farming ecosystem, improve food security and empower farmers as important contributors to India’s self-reliant economy.

## 3. Technology: From UPI to AI and 6G Leadership

Technology and innovation form the third pillar of Saptadhara. PM Modi highlighted India’s success with digital platforms like UPI and called for greater progress in emerging technologies.

He said India must become a global hub for artificial intelligence, robotics, data centres and next-generation technologies, including Made-in-India 6G networks.

## 4. Gati Shakti: Faster Infrastructure and Connectivity

The fourth pillar, Gati Shakti, focuses on improving infrastructure and connectivity across the country.

PM Modi emphasised the need for better roads, expressways and logistics networks to boost economic activity, strengthen businesses and improve India’s competitiveness in global trade.

## 5. Raksha Shakti: Self-Reliant Defence Sector

Defence capability is the fifth pillar of the vision. PM Modi called for expanding domestic defence manufacturing and reducing dependence on imports.

He highlighted the importance of new-age defence technologies such as drones and counter-drone systems to strengthen India’s security capabilities.

## 6. Green Energy: Driving Sustainable Growth

Green energy is the sixth pillar of Saptadhara. PM Modi stressed the need for innovation in renewable energy to meet India’s growing power requirements while protecting the environment.

The focus is on achieving energy security through cleaner sources and creating a sustainable growth model for the future.

## 7. Soft Power: Taking Indian Culture Global

The seventh pillar highlights India’s cultural strength and global influence. PM Modi pointed to yoga, handicrafts, films, animation, gaming, digital content and tourism as important areas of India’s soft power.

He said India’s cultural heritage and creative industries can become major contributors to economic growth and strengthen the country’s global identity.

## Saptadhara: Roadmap Towards Viksit Bharat @2047

Together, the seven pillars of Saptadhara represent an integrated vision for India’s future — combining economic growth, technological advancement, defence strength, environmental responsibility and cultural influence.

The framework aligns with PM Modi’s larger goal of transforming India into a developed, self-reliant and globally influential nation by 2047, when the country completes 100 years of Independence.

## Our Story

##### Our Mission

Pillar Clinical Research provides a professional and honest approach to clinical trials for the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries to accelerate the development of new, safe, and effective medical therapies for the benefit of the volunteers we serve and the broader patient community.

##### Our Vision

Pillar Clinical Research seeks to become *the* volunteer-centered clinical research organization of reference to pharmaceutical and biotechnology sponsors for managing central nervous system clinical trials and developing innovative treatments worldwide.

##### Our Background

Pillar Clinical Research provides expert conduct of early- and late-phase trials for both inpatient and outpatient clinical studies. Founded in 2008, Pillar is distinguished for exceptional participant care, superior research services, and dedication to advancing pharmaceutical development. Pillar is proud of a long history collaborating with industry sponsors, Contract Research Organizations (CROs), industry vendors, and clinical-based technology providers.

#### At Pillar Clinical Research, we see no end to the integrity, innovation, and impact we can provide as an organization. These three principles are interconnected with each other and interwoven throughout everything we achieve.

#### Integrity

Clinical research organizations should prioritize integrity because it serves as the foundation for trust, credibility, and the advancement of science. Integrity ensures that research findings are accurate, unbiased, and reliable, which is essential for developing effective treatments and making informed medical decisions. We care so deeply about integrity because we place such a high value on patient safety, pharmaceutical reliability, and public trust. By upholding the highest ethical standards, Pillar Clinical Research fosters a culture of accountability, transparency, and respect, ensuring that the results of our work contribute positively to the health and well-being of society.

#### Innovation

Innovation in clinical research is a vital value for any research network, as it drives the discovery of new treatments, methodologies, and technologies that improve patient outcomes and advance medical science. By fostering a culture of creativity and forward-thinking, research networks like Pillar Clinical Research can extend the boundaries of traditional approaches, leading to faster and more effective therapies for various conditions. Innovation encourages the exploration of novel ideas safely, the application of cutting-edge technology, and the improvement of clinical trial processes, making research more efficient and accessible. Prioritizing innovation enables us to stay ahead of emerging health challenges, ultimately benefiting patients and the medical community at large.

#### Impact

Impact is a core value for Pillar Clinical Research because it reflects the tangible difference the organization makes in improving public health and advancing medical knowledge. A focus on impact ensures that research efforts are both scientifically sound and also relevant, meaningful, and capable of transforming patient care. By prioritizing impactful studies, we can address pressing health challenges, influence healthcare policies, and shape the future of medicine. This value encourages researchers to pursue outcomes that have real-world benefits, such as new therapies, improved diagnostics, and better prevention strategies. Ultimately, impact ensures that the organization’s work leads to positive changes that resonate across healthcare systems, communities, and the lives of patients.

title: PM Modi unveils seven-pillar 'Sapta Dhara' roadmap for Viksit Bharat
content:
Home / India News / PM Modi unveils seven-pillar 'Sapta Dhara' roadmap for Viksit Bharat

PM Modi unveils seven-pillar 'Sapta Dhara' roadmap for Viksit Bharat

The framework places manufacturing, food processing and technology at its core, alongside infrastructure, defence, the green and blue economy, and India's soft power

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday outlined a seven-pillar development framework, or “Sapta Dhara”, to guide India’s journey towards becoming a developed economy by 2047, placing manufacturing, food processing and technology at the heart of the next phase of economic growth.

In his 80th Independence Day address, Modi said India needed a new growth framework to achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat, identifying seven “streams of strength” that would drive the country’s economic transformation.

“The first shakti of the Sapta Dhara is the manufacturing sector. For this, we need to focus on three things—cost, quality, and scale. There should be no compromise with quality. This will be our brand value,” Modi said.

The emphasis on manufacturing comes as India seeks to raise the sector’s share in gross domestic product (GDP) to 25 per cent by 2035 from around 17 per cent currently. The government aims to position India as a key alternative production base in global supply chains. Modi’s focus on cost, quality and scale echoes broader efforts to improve export competitiveness and attract investment into manufacturing.

The second pillar that the Prime Minister identified for Viksit Bharat was agriculture and food processing. Modi urged industry to leverage the market-access opportunities created by India’s expanding network of free trade agreements (FTAs).

“With the new FTAs, we have access to greater global markets now,” he said, advocating a renewed push towards value addition in agriculture and processed food exports.

In the current financial year so far, New Delhi has put into effect two trade deals — FTAs with Oman and the United Kingdom (UK). The next on the cards is India’s agreement with the European Union (EU), likely to be signed by December and made effective in the first half of next year.

The third pillar highlighted by Modi was technology and innovation, with an emphasis on semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), digital infrastructure and emerging technologies as key drivers of future growth.

Beyond these three areas, Modi outlined four additional pillars under the Sapta Dhara framework: Gati Shakti, aimed at strengthening infrastructure and logistics; defence power, centred on self-reliance in arms manufacturing; the green and blue economy, focused on sustainable growth and marine resources; and India’s soft power, encompassing its cultural, diplomatic and global influence.

Modi said these seven streams would collectively shape India’s development trajectory as it works towards becoming a developed nation by 2047.

The seven-pronged framework reinforces several themes that have featured prominently in recent government policy initiatives, including infrastructure creation, export-led manufacturing, energy transition, technological self-reliance and defence indigenisation.

The emphasis on food processing and manufacturing is particularly significant as India seeks to expand its share in global trade while creating large-scale employment opportunities.

While the Prime Minister did not announce specific policy measures under the “Sapta Dhara” framework, he said the seven-pillar roadmap would offer a broad blueprint for the government’s economic and development priorities in the coming years.

The “Sapta Dhara” can help India achieve in five to seven years what it could not achieve in the past five to seven decades, Modi said.

“Through the power of Sapta Dhara, we will give the nation new heights, new momentum, and the ability to outdo new goals,” he said.

title: PM Modi Unveils 'Sapta Dhara' Vision, Says it Will Drive India's Next Growth Phase
content:
India

# PM Modi Unveils 'Sapta Dhara' Vision, Says it Will Drive India's Next Growth Phase

In his 80th Independence Day address, PM Modi outlined ‘Sapta Dhara’ or seven streams of strength, calling for a stronger manufacturing sector and greater youth participation to drive India’s development.

PM Modi unveils the ‘Sapta Dhara’ vision during his 80th Independence Day address from the Red FortIANS

IANS Agency

Published on:

Aug 15, 2026, 09:30

Follow NewsGram WhatsApp Channel

**PRIME MINISTER NARENDRA MODI,** in his Independence Day address on Saturday, unveiled the concept of 'Sapta Dhara' (Seven Streams), describing seven key areas of strength that he said would provide India with the momentum and capabilities required to achieve the next level of growth and build a 'Viksit Bharat'.

Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort, PM Modi drew a comparison with the historical idea of 'Sapta Sindhu' (Seven Rivers), saying that India now needs a new current of development and national strength to realise its aspirations for a developed India.

"Today, I would also like to recall that era when the nation... when we knew, understood, and heard of India's prowess in the form of the 'Sapta Sindhu' (Seven Rivers). Now, to build a Viksit Bharat, we need a new current. Today, from the ramparts of the Red Fort, I invoke the 'Sapta Dhara' of strength before the nation," the Prime Minister said.

PM Modi said that the next five to seven years would be particularly important, adding that the combined strength of the seven streams could help India achieve in the coming years what could not be accomplished over several previous decades.

He said the country would also fully harness the power and potential of its youth and integrate their capabilities into the process of nation-building.

"Alongside this, the power and potential of our youth will be fully harnessed and integrated into nation-building. In the coming days, when I speak of Sapta Dhara, the very first stream of power is: Manufacturing Power. My dear fellow citizens, we need to significantly propel our manufacturing sector forward. Along with expanding production, we must manufacture both micro-components and large finished products. The entire value chain must belong to us, and we must carry it forward," he said.

The Prime Minister stressed that India needs to develop not only individual components but also complete products and end-to-end manufacturing capabilities. From designing products to producing them, he said, India should establish itself as a "trusted global supply chain hub".

"To my brothers and sisters working in the manufacturing sector -- this is the right time, this is an opportunity. Do not let this opportunity slip away. To achieve this, we must meet global benchmarks in terms of Cost, Quality, and Scale. Our factories must be competitive, our products user-friendly, and our packaging appealing and attractive to people worldwide. 'Zero Defect' and precision manufacturing must become our defining identity," he said.

PM Modi also emphasised the importance of maintaining international standards in manufacturing and called upon entrepreneurs, manufacturers and MSMEs to use the opportunity to expand India's global footprint.

"When it comes to quality, there should be 'No Compromise'. Therefore, our core mantra must be: 'Quality, Quality, Quality'," he added.

The second stream of the 'Sapta Dhara', according to PM Modi, is Agriculture and Food Production, along with large-scale Food Processing. He said India's farmers now have access to expanding global markets and stressed the need to connect agricultural production with international demand.

"Today, world markets have opened up for our farmers. Because of optics and evolving demand, we are gaining access to a huge market; we need to reach there, and we must seize that space. We need to bridge the journey from farm to export market," the Prime Minister said.

The third stream is Technology and Innovation, which PM Modi described as increasingly important in an era shaped by Artificial Intelligence, Quantum technology, space, robotics and data centres.

"Today is the era of AI, Quantum, Space, Robotics, and Data Centres. An entirely new landscape has unfolded. Emerging technologies are challenging us at every single moment. Therefore, India must not merely remain a consumer market for the world; we must become the Global Hub of Innovation," he said.

PM Modi said India had already demonstrated its technological capabilities through UPI and digital public infrastructure and should now work towards taking its digital public technologies to every part of the world.

The fourth stream of the 'Sapta Dhara' is Gati Shakti, which encompasses infrastructure and connectivity.

"Through Gati Shakti, we must focus on seamless, high-speed connectivity across the country. We need to connect cities via high-speed rail, build modern highways, inland waterways, advanced airports, and robust multimodal logistics systems," he added.

The fifth stream is Raksha Shakti, or Defence Power, which PM Modi said remains critical for India's security and strategic autonomy. He stressed that achieving self-reliance in defence is essential and said India cannot continue to depend on other nations for its defence requirements.

"The importance of defence capability is paramount in every sense. My dear citizens, achieving Aatmanirbharta in defence is essential; India and the world have realised that there is no alternative. When the world looks out for itself, India cannot merely remain an arms market for other nations," he said.

The Prime Minister said India must develop next-generation defence technologies and aim to become a Global Defence Supplier. He highlighted the need to develop capabilities in drone systems, counter-drone systems and hypersonic defence technologies.

He also pointed to cybersecurity as an increasingly important area of defence, saying that the capabilities and talent of India's youth could be used to protect both the country and the wider world.

The sixth stream of the 'Sapta Dhara' is the Green Economy and Blue Economy, which PM Modi said would also create new employment opportunities through green jobs.

"We must achieve global scale in Green Hydrogen, Renewable Energy, Energy Storage, Green Mobility, and Green Manufacturing. While the world continues to deliberate on global warming, India is actively discovering pathways and providing practical solutions to challenges. India is leading with immense capability in the global Green Movement," he said.

PM Modi also highlighted the opportunities available in the Blue Economy because of India's extensive coastline. He said sectors such as fisheries, coastal tourism and ocean technologies could play an important role in India's future economic growth.

The seventh and final stream of the 'Sapta Dhara' is India's Soft Power, which the Prime Minister described as an area of immense importance not only for the country but also for the world.

"India's soft power is truly immense. Today, Yoga has connected the entire world to India. Yoga is becoming a source of energy for humanity and a major pillar of trust in India. For a country rich with centres of faith, Ayurveda, holistic healthcare systems, and the 'Heal in India' initiative, we can showcase our strengths to the world through handicrafts, culture, films, our creative ecosystem, VFX, animation, gaming, and digital content. In the creative world, India can establish its pre-eminence," PM Modi said.

He said India must develop its soft power into a global capability and use its cultural, creative and technological strengths to establish a stronger presence internationally.

"India has provided significant momentum to the WAVES Summit (World Audio Visual & Entertainment Summit), a platform the world eagerly looks forward to, presenting India's soft power and creative talent to the entire world," he added.

Through the 'Sapta Dhara' framework, PM Modi underlined the need for India to simultaneously strengthen manufacturing, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, green and blue economies, and soft power as the country works towards achieving the broader vision of a 'Viksit Bharat'.

# PM Modi unveils 'Sapta Dhara' for 'Viksit Bharat': What is his seven-point roadmap

TOI News Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 15, 2026, 13:50 IST

PM Modi delivers his 13th consecutive Independence Day speech from Red Fort. (PTI)

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday announced “Sapta Dhara” - a seven-point reform framework that will accelerate India’s march towards its goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047.Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi recalled the era when India's might was known through the "Sapta Sindhu" and said the country now needs new streams of strength to build a developed India."Today, from the ramparts of the Red Fort, I invoke the seven streams of power before the nation," PM Modi said and identified seven areas of focus.

PM Modi's Sapta Dhara for Viksit Bharat

"In the coming 5-7 years, with the strength and power of these seven streams, we will give the country new heights, new momentum, and the capacity to achieve new goals," PM Modi said, adding that the full potential of the nation's youth power will be utilised in nation-building.

## Manufacturing Power

The first strength of the 'Sapta Dhara' is manufacturing power, PM Modi said, stressing the need to take the manufacturing sector forward and produce both small components and large products. "We must build a complete value chain. From design to manufacturing, India must establish itself as a trusted global supply chain partner for the world," he said."We must rise to global standards of cost, quality and scale," the Prime Minister said.He said Indian manufacturers must meet global benchmarks on cost, quality and scale, while factories should be competitive, products user-friendly and packaging attractive."For every manufacturer, every entrepreneur, every MSME, I want to say that in the global market, our identity should be based on trust and quality," PM Modi said, stressing that there should be "no compromise" on quality.

##

## Agriculture and food processing

PM Modi defined the second stream as agriculture and food processing and called Indian farmers to access global markets."The world's markets are now open for our farmers. Due to FTAs, we are gaining access to a very large market. We must reach there," PM Modi said, stressing the need to go "from the farm to the export market".The Prime Minister said traditional cuisine, millets, spices, fruits and flowers and chemical-free agricultural produce could become global brands, provided they meet international parameters.

## Technology and innovation

Stating the third stream as technology and innovation, PM Modi said India must become an innovation hub as emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, quantum technology, space, robotics and data centres create new opportunities."We have made our mark in UPI and digital public infrastructure," PM Modi said, calling for India's digital public technologies to be taken to every corner of the world."India must lead in next-generation communication technology. Made in India 6G should reach every corner; this should be our goal," PM Modi said.

## Gati Shakti

Defining the fourth strength of the 'Sapta Dhara' as Gati Shakti, PM Modi stressed the need for seamless and high-speed connectivity. "Our cities must be connected through high speed rail," he said.PM Modi also called for a focus on port-led development, saying ports should not remain merely places for loading and unloading goods but should become engines of growth.

## Defence power

The PM highlighted defence power as the fifth strength, stressing the need for self-reliance in the defence sector and for India to emerge as a global supplier of next-generation defence technologies."When the world is thinking about itself, India cannot remain merely a market for the world," he said."We have to become global suppliers. We have to take leadership in hypersonic defence technologies," PM Modi said.He also called for developing drones, counter-drone systems and hypersonic defence technologies, while underlining the growing importance of cyber security. "India has to become self-reliant in the defence sector."

## Green and blue economy

PM Modi said the sixth stream is the green and blue economy, which will also create green jobs.He called for India to operate at a global scale in green hydrogen, renewable energy, energy storage, green mobility and green manufacturing, while continuing to provide solutions to global challenges.The Prime Minister also highlighted opportunities in the blue economy, including fisheries, coastal tourism and ocean technology, given India's long coastline.

# PM Modi’s ‘Sapta Dhara’ blueprint: New semiconductor plants, 100 GW nuclear target and quality-first manufacturing drive India’s ‘Viksit Bharat’ push

## Independence Day 2026: PM Modi announced that one crore youth will be trained in artificial intelligence skilling courses. He also added that free online coaching will be provided to youth preparing for various competitive examinations.

Written by Sheenu Sharma

Updated:  August 15, 2026 10:49 IST

Follow Us

Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

On the occasion of the 80th Independence Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi used his Red Fort address to lay out a seven-point “Sapta Dhara” (seven streams) roadmap to turn India into a developed nation by 2047. This roadmap links energy security, advanced manufacturing and self-reliance in chips, critical minerals and defence to the country’s next growth leap.

“A nation becomes great and achieves its goals when it moves forward driven by its dreams, its resolve, and its inherent strength. Small dreams will no longer suffice. We must dream big, for big dreams expand our thinking and broaden the horizons of our vision,” he said, framing the push for Viksit Bharat around concrete sectors like semiconductors, nuclear power, data centres, railways, aviation and green-blue economy.

> Addressing the nation on Independence Day.https://t.co/Q67F6cB96x
>
> — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) August 15, 2026

## Sapta Dhara: Manufacturing, food processing and tech innovation as core engines

PM Modi said the first “shakti” of the Sapta Dhara is the manufacturing sector, where India must focus on “cost, quality and scale,” warning that “there should be no compromise with quality. This will be our brand value.”

The second stream is agriculture and food processing, which he tied to new Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) that now give Indian MSMEs access to larger global markets.

The third is technology, innovation and digital technologies, with a clear emphasis on chips, AI and data infrastructure as the backbone of the new economy.

> 80वें स्वतंत्रता दिवस के अवसर पर लाल किले की प्राचीर से पीएम मोदी ने किया शक्ति की सप्तधारा का आह्वान…
>
> – मैन्युफैक्चरिंग पावर  
> – कृषि और फूड प्रोसेसिंग   
> – Technology और Innovation   
> – गति शक्ति   
> – रक्षा शक्ति  
> – ग्रीन इकोनॉमी और ब्लू इकोनॉमी  
> – सॉफ्ट पावर#IndiaIndependenceDay… pic.twitter.com/8jEup8OTTh
>
> — BJP (@BJP4India) August 15, 2026

“In today’s digital world and the age of technology, we understand the importance of chips. Whether it is electronic goods, medical equipment or transportation systems, chips are indispensable to all of them. Without chips, the entire world could come to a standstill,” he said.

## Semiconductors: New plants already operational, 5–8 more in 7–8 years

On semiconductors, PM Modi announced that three major semiconductor plants have already been set up in India and that production from these facilities has begun, including for exports.

“I want to tell my fellow citizens that in the next seven to eight years, another five to eight semiconductor plants are likely to become operational very soon. This journey towards an Aatmanirbhar Bharat is paving the way for us to move towards a Viksit Bharat,” he said.

This push is backed by a parallel focus on critical minerals, which are essential for chips, batteries and advanced electronics, with the government positioning India as an emerging supplier that other countries are now looking to for secure mineral supply chains.

## Energy security: 100 GW nuclear by 2047, 5 reactors this decade, SHANTI Act

PM Narendra Modi flagged energy security as “the demand of our time,” noting that running the new world is “difficult even without energy” and that “we will need a very large amount of electricity for chips, AI, and data centers.” He said nuclear energy is a “major means of energy security” and that Parliament has passed the “Peace Act” (referred to in his speech as the SHANTI Act) to create the legal framework for a major nuclear expansion.

“By 2047, we are moving forward with the target of 100 GW of nuclear power. We aim to commission five new nuclear reactors within this decade alone,” he said, adding that India this year achieved a significant milestone by mastering fast breeder nuclear technology, a key step toward self-reliance in nuclear fuel.

## Electrification, railways and hydrogen trains: From 30% in 90 years to 100% in a decade

On railways, PM Modi contrasted past and present progress to underline the new pace of development. “Railway electrification in India began in 1925. Yet, over nearly 90 years, only 30% of the railway network had been electrified. In just the last decade, India has achieved 100% railway electrification,” he said.

This has cut dependence on imported diesel and supported a cleaner environment, while also enabling new technologies like India’s first hydrogen-powered train, which he highlighted as part of the broader push for green mobility and high-speed, seamless connectivity under the “Gati-shakti” stream of Sapta Dhara.

> The seventh strength of the Saptadhara is India’s soft power.
>
> Today, Yoga has connected the entire world with India.
>
> Yoga is becoming a source of energy for the world and a major source of trust in India.
>
> These seven strengths are not merely a pathway to progress in individual… pic.twitter.com/GF7ecFef0v
>
> — BJP (@BJP4India) August 15, 2026

## Gati-shakti connectivity and defence as a global supplier

The fourth “shakti” is “Gati-shakti” – seamless, high-speed connectivity across rail, roads, inland waterways, airports, multi-modal logistics hubs and ports, with a strong emphasis on port-led development. The fifth stream is defence production, where Modi said India must not only become self-reliant but also emerge as a global supplier by leveraging next-generation defence technologies.

“The world has realised that there is no alternative to self-reliance in defence… We have to become ‘aatmanirbhar’ in the defence sector; we have to become a global supplier by leveraging next generation defence technology,” he said.

He noted that defence production has risen nearly fourfold in the last 12 years, alongside 21-fold growth in modern railway coach production and 33-fold growth in mobile phone manufacturing.

## Green-blue economy and soft power as global differentiators

The sixth stream is the green economy, covering renewable energy, energy storage, green manufacturing and the blue economy, including opportunities in offshore and marine resources. Modi recalled that nearly 99% of India’s marine area had earlier been declared a “No Go Area” for exploration, a “poverty of thought” that his government has reversed by turning these into “Go Ahead Areas” to boost energy and resource security.

The seventh “shakti” is India’s soft power – yoga, Ayurveda, holistic healthcare, handicrafts, culture, films, animation, gaming and digital content – which he said is being leveraged through initiatives like the WAVES summit and the country’s more than 100 national parks to attract tourists and strengthen India’s global brand.

## Data centres, AI skilling and digital public tech: Powering the chip-AI era

Linking chips to data infrastructure, Narendra Modi said the world now needs huge amounts of electricity for chips, AI and data centres, making energy security and digital infrastructure two sides of the same coin. In this context, he announced that one crore youth will be enrolled in an AI skill programme over the next year, alongside free education and coaching support for poor families, to ensure India has the talent pipeline for an AI-driven economy.

He also stressed the need to take India’s digital public technologies to every corner of the world, saying, “We have to take digital public technologies to every corner of the world; it should be our aim to take made in India 6G everywhere,” positioning Indian digital stacks as global public goods.

## Manufacturing quality, FTAs and MSMEs: “No compromise on quality”

PM Modi returned repeatedly to the theme of quality in manufacturing, insisting that cost and scale cannot come at the expense of standards. “The first ‘shakti’ of the Sapta Dhara is manufacturing sector. For this initiative, we need to focus on three things – cost, quality and scale. There should be no compromise with quality. This will be our brand value,” he said.

He urged MSMEs to make full use of the FTAs India has signed with nearly 40 countries since 2014, calling them a “massive opening” for Indian textiles, machinery, pharmaceuticals and other products to reach global markets. “I want to tell our MSMEs that we must not miss this opportunity. We must reach out to the global market,” he said.

On governance, PM Modi said thousands of compliance requirements have been eliminated and hundreds of archaic laws repealed, arguing that “India cannot march forward in the 21st century by relying on laws of the previous century.”

## PM urges youth to help make census more accurate via correct data

He also made a direct appeal to young people to actively participate in the ongoing Census exercise, asking them to help provide correct digital information about their families to make the census error-free.

PM also warned that while armed Naxals have been largely eliminated from forests, “‘Dimagi Naxals’ remain.” He described them as people with a Maoist mindset who try to drag society down the wrong path and must be isolated so that youth can align with the mainstream Viksit Bharat effort.

## From “Fragile Five” to fast-growing major economy: The 12-year turnaround

PM Modi contrasted India’s position in 2014, when it was grouped among the “Fragile Five”, with its current status as the world’s fastest-growing major economy, crediting the last 12 years for a decisive change in pace and mindset. “We were in the Fragile Five. Now we are a major and fast-growing economy. We could not push ourselves earlier. We were stuck,” he said, adding that “it is now impossible to come in the way of the resolve of 140 crore Indians.”

He cited fourfold growth in defence production, fivefold in Khadi and village industries, sevenfold in electronics manufacturing, 21-fold in modern railway coaches and 33-fold in mobile phone production as evidence of this shift.

## Social contracts: Urea, DAP, gas, water, toilets and housing at accelerated pace

On social welfare, PM Modi highlighted that while global urea prices soared to around Rs 3,000 per sack, Indian farmers continue to get it at Rs 300, with the government absorbing the difference; similarly, DAP is being supplied at Rs 1,350 despite global prices near Rs 5,000.

He also noted that piped gas coverage has expanded from 70 cities to 700 in 12 years, with 1.75 crore households now connected, and that tap-water connections, toilets for the poor and housing for the underprivileged have been delivered at 15, four and three times the previous annual rates respectively. These gains, he argued, rest on a “citizens first” approach that kept people at the centre even through crises like the pandemic and geopolitical shocks.

## Aviation, ports and logistics: Building the infrastructure spine for trade and industry

Though not enumerated as a separate “shakti”, aviation, ports and logistics featured prominently under Gati-shakti and port-led development, with PM Narendra Modi stressing seamless high-speed rail, modern highways, inland waterways, new airports, multi-modal logistics hubs and expanded metro networks as the infrastructure spine for manufacturing and trade.

The push on ports and logistics is designed to lower costs, improve export competitiveness and integrate India more deeply into global supply chains, especially as the country leverages its FTAs and positions itself as a reliable alternative in a world where “every nation has shifted towards a mindset of looking after its own interests.”

## “Put country before self”: The call for a new work culture and national mission

Closing his Sapta Dhara narrative, PM Modi called for a change in work culture and thinking, urging citizens to put national interest and duty above self. “Let us put country before self; national interest and sense of duty should be our identity, this is India’s hour,” he said.

He framed the seven streams – manufacturing; agriculture and food processing; technology and innovation; Gati-shakti; defence; green and blue economy; and soft power – as the new current needed to build Viksit Bharat by 2047, with semiconductors, critical minerals, electrification, data centres, quality-first manufacturing, modern railways and aviation as the concrete pillars of that transformation.

This article was first uploaded on August fifteen, twenty twenty-six, at fifty-two minutes past nine in the morning.

title: 'Raksha Shakti' to soft power: PM Modi lays out 'Sapta Dhara' vision to build Viksit Bharat by 2047; Opposition says Govt "crushing the poor"
